head: 807860fa1d60c7d8e82022cf67036cdc484a71da
classification_reasons: Blast radius: the change touches the risk-list item 'auth', the runbook Go's authorization in the step that holds the runbook secrets. Round 4 also adds a case key, framework_root, to the shared eval runner plugin/evals/run.py.

The spec is tight: R1-R10 are measurable and every flagged concern is closed. The round-4 runner mechanism is outside spec.md's 'one file of the plugin changes'. It comes from the owner's review 5778239621 on PR #405, and plan.md lists it.

Coverage: the reproducing tests in tests/test_detect_cli.py failed before the fix (failing-test.log), and tests/test_evals.py adds a test of framework_root. Both are pre-existing test files in a fix-type change, edited as the owner asked and as panel decision 1 declared.
attempted: Intent: _human_label_actor now refuses an actor that fails is_owner_actor(actor, config, None, repo), after the bot/automation branch, and cmd_go (detect/cli.py:1218-1222) passes the default branch's copy from _approved_config. That closes the finding at detect/cli.py:1183 itself, not a nearby problem. The label is left in place, the job still exits 0, and the refusal names the label, the actor and the owner's account (R1, R5, R6).

Owner's request 5778239621, checked item by item. (a) framework_root is applied only when run_case gets framework_suite=args.fixture; a --root suite returns the reason before any copy or session. (b) A test of the mechanism is added. (c) The whole-suite python -m pytest check is dropped and the targeted -k command kept. (d) The lesson_and_eval gate check is not in the diff. (e) The OPERATING_MODEL.md sdlc-runbook.yml row (line 98) now says the actor must be the owner's account (is_owner_actor, the default branch's sdlc.yaml, since 1.0.51). All five are applied, and nothing beyond them.

Spec and plan: every code and doc file in the diff is listed in plan.md 'Files that change'. That covers marketplace.json on its own line (8cd193f), plugin.json, OPERATING_MODEL.md, the eval case, both lessons files, detect/cli.py, run.py and both test files. 'Order of work' covers only the original fix steps; the round-4 lines live under Files and Proof. Nit: fix-response.md ends at round 3 and has no round-4 section answering request 5778239621. That is process, not behavior.

Proof: test.log (2888 passed), build.log, lint.log and verifier.md all date from 2026-11-04T19:44:55Z or earlier. They prove the detect/cli.py fix but predate 4958e80, so none of them names test_framework_root_runs_setup_and_commands_in_the_framework_only_in_its_suite. The session ran tests/test_evals.py (79 passed, as reported, not committed), and the runner replaces the three logs on HEAD after the session. I leave those logs to the runner and cite them neither for nor against this round.

The tests, trying to break them: the new test_evals test fails if setup runs in the workspace, because framework/made.txt would be absent and the workspace's made.txt exists:false check would fail. It fails if the command check runs in the workspace, because marker.txt exists only in the framework root. It asserts the session cwd is 'project', that a --root suite returns 1 with no session logged and the exact reason, and that a non-bool framework_root is a problem. It cannot pass with the mechanism broken. The detect tests: the head case proves the head's owner is ignored, and the main case proves the-owner is refused before the named owner's Go runs, so the 'did not ask for Go' reason cannot mask the check.

Eval case 0006: if the -k expression selects nothing, pytest exits 5 and the case fails. command_chain uses shlex without a shell, so the quoted -k stays one argument. Nit: if only the two new tests were renamed, test_go_by_a_person_runs_the_runbook alone would keep the case green. The output regex '\d+ passed' reads the agent's answer in the fixture, which the fixture's own pytest satisfies, so it adds little but breaks nothing. The command check is the real guard.

Running the command in CI: framework-evals.yml runs run.py --fixture and installs pytest. tests/test_detect_cli.py, conftest.py and fixture_repos need no pyyaml, since the plugin uses state.yamlish. pyproject sets pythonpath plugin and '.' with testpaths tests, so the command works from the framework root. check_env is the same environment the workspace commands already get.

Blast radius of framework_root: setup and command checks get no new capability; only the working directory changes, and the env is the same. Cases are the framework repository's own. Projects call run.py via evals/check.py with --root, never --fixture, so a project case using the key fails closed. The evaluate() and run_case() parameters are keyword arguments with defaults, and main is the only caller passing framework_suite. One side effect: a framework_root case's setup writes into the framework checkout and is not cleaned up. That is documented by the test and unused by case 0006, which has no setup.

Claims against the code: is_owner_actor(actor, config, env=None, repo=None) and owner_login in plugin/state/unpark.py match the call and the order R2 states (sdlc.yaml owner, GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, --repo, else None, failing closed). _approved_config returns approved_files' default-branch copy. The OPERATING_MODEL row and the lesson's Prevention (fixed in a2ad922: targeted tests in the framework root, failing on a failure or on no match) match the diff. Nit: the module docstring at plugin/detect/cli.py:28 still says 'a person must have applied it', which is now narrower in practice (the owner's account). It is outside the diff and not behavior.

Policies: no credential in the added lines, no new dependency, and no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) in the diff. The version is bumped in plugin.json and marketplace.json together. No existing test's body or assertion changed in test_detect_cli.py (one declared fixture line) or test_evals.py (one list entry the owner requested, one new test).
Skip markers: none added in the diff.
Drive: commands.drive does not apply. There is no product drive and no evidence/proof/.

Risk item 'auth': the item is the change's purpose and narrows who can authorize the Go. The owner accepted it at design (PR #403), and this round does not change the authorization code. Per the delegation prompt, the brief is written by the separate pass.
